about.text: Skimmed milk dried, mostly by spraying it into hot air, to a fine powder with no more than 1.5 % fat, which keeps for up to three years if stored cool and dry. Used in bread and cakes, confectionery and infant formula, and mixed back with water as milk where fresh milk is scarce. Used in chocolate and infant formula, shipped as UN food aid, and even stood in for cocaine on film sets.

how.text: Skimmed milk is heated to a chosen class, boiled down to about half solids under vacuum and sprayed into hot air to a dry powder.

steps.note: To a chosen class: low-heat 75 °C for 15 s, medium-heat 90–100 °C for 20 s, high-heat 120 °C for 120 s, heat-stable high-heat 125 °C for 180 s.
Under vacuum to 48–51 % total solids, the lower the hotter the heat class.
Sprayed into hot air that enters at 200–230 °C and leaves at 80–85 °C.
